introduction-running-out-of-vlans.core: VLAN IDs are 12 bits (4,094 usable), far too few for multi-tenant clouds and large data centres, and VLANs require a stretched L2 across the physical network, inheriting STP and broadcast problems. Overlays encapsulate tenant L2/L3 traffic inside UDP/IP packets over a routed underlay. That gives millions of segments, L2 over L3, and decouples virtual networks from the physical topology.

first_principles.problem: A cloud provider needs 50,000 isolated tenant networks on a routed leaf-spine fabric.

analogy.title: Shipping containers on a rail network
analogy.story: Any cargo (tenant traffic) goes into standard containers on standard rails (IP), with millions of container IDs.
analogy.breaks: Containers are physical; encapsulation adds header bytes.

check.q: How many segments can VXLAN identify?

underlay-vs-overlay.core: The underlay is the physical routed network (leaf-spine with BGP or OSPF and ECMP) whose job is simply to deliver IP packets between tunnel endpoints quickly and reliably. The overlay is the virtual network tenants see, built from tunnels between endpoints. Keeping them separate means the underlay is simple and stable while overlays are created and changed in software, but troubleshooting must consider both layers.

first_principles.problem: Tenant traffic drops intermittently, and the team can't tell whether the virtual network or the physical fabric is at fault.
truths: Encapsulation hides inner details from the underlay.
derivation: Design the **underlay** for IP reachability + ECMP.
Correlate **outer and inner** headers when debugging.

analogy.title: Roads and delivery routes
analogy.story: The road network (underlay) must be sound; delivery companies (overlays) design routes on top without rebuilding roads.
analogy.breaks: Delivery firms see road closures; overlays only see tunnel failures.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: See both layers in one packet.

code.text:
tcpdump -ni eth0 udp port 4789 -vv
# outer: 10.0.1.11 > 10.0.2.12 UDP 4789 (underlay)
#   VXLAN vni 5001
#   inner: 192.168.10.5 > 192.168.10.9 ICMP echo (overlay)

check.q: Why do VXLAN tunnel endpoints vary the outer UDP source port?
check.a: To provide entropy so the underlay's ECMP hashing spreads different inner flows across multiple paths.

vxlan-the-standard-overlay.core: VXLAN (RFC 7348) wraps an Ethernet frame in an 8-byte VXLAN header carrying a 24-bit VNI, inside UDP (port 4789), IP and an outer Ethernet header, about 50 bytes of overhead. It's supported everywhere: Linux, switches, NSX and Kubernetes CNIs like Flannel and Calico. Endpoints learn remote MACs by flood-and-learn via multicast or, preferably, via a BGP EVPN control plane.

first_principles.problem: A data centre needs L2 tenant segments across racks without stretching VLANs through the spine.
truths: Ethernet frames can ride inside UDP.
Learning MAC locations needs a mechanism.
derivation: Encapsulate: **Eth / IP / UDP 4789 / VXLAN / inner Eth**.

analogy.title: Putting a sealed letter inside a courier envelope
analogy.story: The courier only reads the outer envelope's address; the recipient opens it to find the original letter with its own address.
analogy.breaks: Couriers don't charge per gram of envelope; every VXLAN packet carries 50 extra bytes.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: L2 segment 100 spans hosts over routed underlay.

code.text:
ip link add vxlan100 type vxlan id 100 dstport 4789 local 10.0.1.11 nolearning
ip link set vxlan100 master br100 && ip link set vxlan100 up
bridge fdb append 00:00:00:00:00:00 dev vxlan100 dst 10.0.2.12   # head-end replication

check.q: What UDP port does VXLAN use by default?

vteps-the-tunnel-endpoints.core: VXLAN Tunnel Endpoints (VTEPs) encapsulate and decapsulate traffic. They can be software in hypervisors and hosts (Linux, OVS, Cilium) or hardware in top-of-rack switches. A VTEP must know which remote VTEP hosts each MAC/IP in a VNI. BGP EVPN distributes that (type-2 MAC/IP routes, type-3 for BUM replication), enabling ARP suppression and distributed anycast gateways, which avoids flood-and-learn.

first_principles.problem: Flood-and-learn VXLAN floods unknown traffic to every VTEP, wasting bandwidth at scale.
truths: A control plane can advertise locations.

analogy.title: Post offices with a shared address directory
analogy.story: Instead of shouting at every office 'who has this resident?', offices publish who lives where.
analogy.breaks: Directories update slowly; EVPN updates on every VM move.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: VTEPs learn remote MACs via BGP; no flooding.

code.text:
router bgp 65001
 neighbor SPINES peer-group
 neighbor SPINES remote-as external
 address-family l2vpn evpn
  neighbor SPINES activate
  advertise-all-vni
!
# show bgp l2vpn evpn route type macip

check.q: What does an EVPN type-2 route advertise?
check.a: A MAC (and optionally IP) address and the VTEP/VNI behind which it lives.

the-mtu-headache-encapsulation-tax.core: Encapsulation adds bytes: VXLAN about 50, Geneve 50 or more with options, IPsec around 60. If the underlay MTU is 1500 and the inner packet is 1500, the outer packet is about 1550 and gets dropped or fragmented. Symptoms are classic: pings and small requests work, but large transfers, TLS handshakes with big certificates, or SSH sessions hang. The overlay must either shrink the inner MTU or the underlay must grow.

first_principles.problem: Pods can curl small endpoints, but image pulls and large API responses hang after enabling a VXLAN CNI.

analogy.title: Fitting a full-size box into a slightly bigger box that won't fit the door
analogy.story: The outer box is too big for the doorway, so large deliveries get stuck while small parcels pass.
analogy.breaks: Delivery drivers notice; networks silently drop.

code.text:
# inside pod (MTU 1500, underlay 1500)
ping -M do -s 1472 10.244.2.7   # fails/silent
ping -M do -s 1422 10.244.2.7   # works → effective path ~1450

check.q: Why do small pings succeed while large transfers hang in an MTU mismatch?
check.a: Small packets fit even after encapsulation; only full-size packets exceed the underlay MTU and get dropped.

solving-the-mtu-problem.core: Fix the encapsulation tax in one of two ways. Raise the underlay MTU (9000 jumbo frames in data centres, 9001 in AWS VPCs) so 1500-byte inner packets fit with room to spare. Or lower the inner MTU (1450 for VXLAN) on overlay interfaces and pods, often with TCP MSS clamping at gateways for traffic entering from outside. Also ensure ICMP 'fragmentation needed' passes for PMTUD, and verify end-to-end.

first_principles.problem: A CNI uses 1500 inner MTU over a 1500 underlay, and production traffic stalls.
truths: Either the outer can grow or the inner can shrink.

analogy.title: Widening the door or using smaller boxes
analogy.story: Either enlarge the doorway or pack goods in slightly smaller inner boxes so the outer box fits.
analogy.breaks: Doors are fixed per building; every hop's MTU must match.

code.text:
# shrink inner MTU (Calico)
kubectl patch felixconfiguration default --type merge -p '{"spec":{"vxlanMTU":1450}}'
# clamp MSS at gateway
iptables -t mangle -A FORWARD -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu
# or raise underlay
ip link set eth0 mtu 9000

check.q: What does TCP MSS clamping do?
check.a: Rewrites the MSS option in SYN packets so endpoints send segments small enough to fit the path after encapsulation.

geneve-vxlan-20.core: Geneve (RFC 8926) is a generic overlay encapsulation over UDP 6081 with a 24-bit VNI and variable-length TLV options. The options carry metadata such as security policy IDs, telemetry and service-chain context, without inventing a new protocol for each need. OVN/OVS, VMware NSX-T, AWS Gateway Load Balancer and Cilium use it. VXLAN remains more widely supported in hardware.

first_principles.problem: A virtual network platform needs to carry policy group IDs with each packet, which VXLAN's fixed header can't express.
derivation: Use **VXLAN** where hardware VTEPs need it.

analogy.title: A shipping container with a flexible label pouch
analogy.story: Instead of a fixed label, you can add extra tags (handling, customs, tracking) as needs change.
analogy.breaks: Label pouches are free; options cost MTU and parsing.

code.text:
ip link add gnv0 type geneve id 5001 remote 10.0.2.12 dstport 6081
ip link set gnv0 up
# AWS GWLB sends traffic to appliances encapsulated in Geneve with flow cookie options

check.q: What advantage does Geneve have over VXLAN?
check.a: Variable-length TLV options that carry arbitrary metadata (policy, telemetry) without a new protocol.
